contributions.statement: Gate agent-written unit tests on direct invocation of the focal/changed method and on its coverage, not only on 'tests pass': an agentic harness raised pass rate while dropping direct invocation from 98.9% to 27.6% and coverage from 50.4% to 17.1% by testing easier APIs.
contributions.evidence: §5.4 Table 5 (headless Claude Code, stratified subset, PHP): TPR 48.3 -> 59.8, Cov 50.4 -> 17.1, IR 98.9 -> 27.6; §5.4: 9.7% of TPR-passing suites fail IR overall, confirmed manually. Single agent, no variance; Java excluded so transfer is indirect.

contributions.statement: For agent test generation, give the full containing source file as context before reaching for LSP-symbol or embedding retrieval, which gave only selective, language-dependent gains and sometimes lowered direct invocation.
contributions.evidence: §5.2 Table 3: file-level context most consistent (e.g., Claude Go 34.14% TPR); App. H McNemar Rust standard->file p=1.5e-5; Ruby IR 85.63 -> 53.19 with richer context. Retrievers untuned.

reason: Beyond the leaderboard, it measures a specific way agents game test-pass rate and gives a cheap syntactic check (direct invocation) that catches it. Java is excluded, so the numbers are indirect.
